picks.showTitle: The Catechism in a Year (with Fr. Mike Schmitz)
picks.title: Day 244: The Virtue of Charity (2026)
picks.summary:
The greatest of all the theological virtues is charity. Fr. Mike explains that charity, or love, is to love God above all things for his own sake and to love our neighbor as ourselves. This includes loving our enemies and also obeying God's commandments, two actions that are not always easy. Most importantly, today's readings remind us that true charity is not loving the Father as servants in fear or as mercenaries looking for a reward but rather as his beloved children responding to him who "first loved us." Today's readings are Catechism paragraphs 1822-1829.

picks.title: Radical Love & God's Covenant: Dr. Marcus Peter on Not Finished Yet
picks.summary: Is the idea that "God is love" actually a radical, revolutionary truth? Dr. Marcus Peter—theologian, author, and host of Ave Maria in the Afternoon—joins host Ken Huck on Driving Home the Faith to discuss his book, Not Finished Yet. Drawing from his experience growing up in Malaysia and his journey from atheism to the Catholic Church, Dr. Peter contrasts the Christian revelation of God as eternal, self-giving Love with other worldviews, reminding us never to take the Gospel for granted. picks.title: #337 Cardinal Burke - The Old Testament
picks.summary:
Raymond Leo Cardinal Burke is an American cardinal, canon lawyer, and one of the Catholic Church’s most prominent defenders of traditional doctrine and liturgy. He previously served as Archbishop of St. Louis and as Prefect of the Apostolic Signatura, the Church’s highest judicial court, before being elevated to the College of Cardinals by Pope Benedict XVI in 2010. He is also the founder of the Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe in La Crosse, Wisconsin.

picks.showTitle: The Rosary in a Year (with Fr. Mark-Mary Ames)
picks.title: Day 245: The Sorrowful and Glorious Mysteries
picks.summary:
We continue to build spiritual endurance through the rhythm of daily prayer. Meditating first on the carrying of the cross and the crucifixion and death of Jesus, we enter deeply into his suffering and sacrifice. Then, we transition into hope as we pray the first Glorious Mystery, the Resurrection of our Lord. This movement from sorrow to triumph invites us to reflect on both the cost of redemption and the promise of eternal life. Today’s focus is the mysteries of the Carrying of the Cross, the Crucifixion, and the Resurrection. We will be praying three decades of the Rosary.
